advances: A conditional common conservative selector for a physically realizable finite buffered cover. The lower branch retains inside body loss and drops its positive hinge, and the centroid identity averages contact occurrences.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
In each proper group, a branch consists of one contact $a$ and a tuple of outside densities $\theta_j\in[0,1]$. By the conservative inverse formula the branch gives a linear form with coefficient $1/B_i$ on $A_{ia}$ and weights $\gamma_{ij}=(\rho_{ij}/T_{ij})/B_i$ on the terms $B_{ij}^{\theta}(v)-m_{ij}^{\theta}\cdot\nu_{ij}$, where $B_i=\sum_j\rho_{ij}/T_{ij}$ and $T_{ij}=S_{ij}+\int_{\rm out}\theta_j\,dS/\|u_{ij}\|$. The group's loss is the infimum over these branches. Subtract $\beta D$ from each branch and each atomic row. The disjoint union of all proper branch sets and atomic rows is compact: there are finitely many discrete choices and each density interval is weak-star compact in the dual of $L^1$ of its finite face measure. Each test yields a continuous branch evaluation because the speeds and affine coordinates are integrable and each $T_{ij}$ is uniformly bounded below by $S_{ij}>0$.

For any finite list of tests, take the compact convex hull of their branch-evaluation vectors in the corresponding finite Euclidean space. If this hull were disjoint from the closed nonpositive orthant, strict separation would give a nonnegative linear combination of test coordinates whose value on every branch is strictly positive. The combined direction is actual by finite addability. Its conservative and atomic responses would all be strictly positive, contradicting local minimality. Thus there is a probability mixture of branches nonpositive on the finite list. Probability measures on the compact branch space are weakly compact (the density balls are metrizable on these finite Borel face spaces because $L^1$ is separable). Each prescribed test is weakly closed in this space. The finite intersection property gives one mixture for the entire test class.

For group $i$ define $\kappa_{ia}$ by integrating $1/B_i$ over its branches of contact $a$, and $\omega_{ij}$ by integrating $\gamma_{ij}$ over all its branches. The effective outside density is the average weighted by $\gamma_{ij}$ divided by $\omega_{ij}$. The weighted coarea and first moment aggregate linearly, so
$$
\omega_{ij}T_{ij}=\int\gamma_{ij}T_{ij}^{\rm branch}
=\rho_{ij}\kappa_i .
$$
Also $\sum_j\omega_{ij}=\eta_i$ and all these weights are positive for a positive group. If a finite mixture description is desired, the common effective tuple itself can be paired with contact $a$ at weight $\kappa_{ia}\sum_j\rho_{ij}/T_{ij}$. Summing those weights gives $\eta_i$ and their branch coefficients are exactly the aggregated ones. This also shows that the same selected outside density enters the body, coarea, and section moment.

The coefficient of the free signed variable $\nu_{ij}$ in the aggregated inequality is
$$
\rho_{ij}\sum_a\kappa_{ia}Y_{ia}
-\omega_{ij}T_{ij}\bar w_{ij}
-\rho_{ij}e_i(0,\nabla\Gamma(u_{ij})) .
$$
The pure normal tests of both signs force it to be zero. Use $\nabla\Gamma(u_{ij})=\Sigma u_{ij}$ at $\Gamma(u_{ij})=1$. The coarea relation then gives the asserted mean. The different contact budget coefficients are retained in the mean; the response does not yield one common section barycenter for each individual contact.

statement:
Use the actual finite-group continuation of the full-space finite-contact response lemma, with a complete proper and possibly pure-base atomic covering menu at an attained unpenalized local minimum $\beta=Q/M$. Let the set of joint body and raw parameter directions be a cone closed under finite addition of actual paths. Each such test permits all independent signed cap-normal velocities shared over the contacts in each group. Let $\ell_i^0$ be the proper conservative loss and use the actual loss for each atomic cap. Suppose simultaneous strict improvement of all normalized responses (loss minus $\beta D$) would yield strict actual descent by this cover.

There is one separator for all tests. It has atomic weights $\eta_A\ge0$, cap weights $\omega_{ij}\ge0$, and nonnegative contact weights $\kappa_{ia}$, with $\sum_{ij}\omega_{ij}+\sum_A\eta_A=1$. At each proper group of positive total weight $\eta_i=\sum_j\omega_{ij}$, every cap weight is positive. Its effective outside selector $\theta_{ij}$ satisfies $0\le\theta_{ij}\le1$ and is used both in the body weight and in the section coarea, which on the outside face is $\theta_{ij}\,dS/\|u_{ij}\|$. The inside-support body and section selectors are respectively $1$ and $0$. If $T_{ij}$ is the total allocated coarea and $\bar w_{ij}$ its full physical mean, put $\kappa_i=\sum_a\kappa_{ia}$, $e_{ia}=\varepsilon f_a\kappa_{ia}$, $e_i=\sum_a e_{ia}$. Then
$$
\omega_{ij}T_{ij}=\kappa_i\rho_{ij},\qquad
\bar w_{ij}=\frac{\sum_a\kappa_{ia}Y_{ia}}{\kappa_i}
-\frac{e_i}{\kappa_i}(0,\Sigma u_{ij}).
$$
In the separator's linear inequality the body terms have the allocated cap weights and the proper contact terms have budget coefficients $\kappa_{ia}$. More explicitly, with $B_{ij}^{\theta}(v)=B_{ij}(v)+\int_{\rm out}\theta_{ij}v\,dS$ and $m_{ij}^{\theta}=T_{ij}\bar w_{ij}$, the proper terms before the common $-\beta D$ are
$$
\sum_{ij}\omega_{ij}\bigl(B_{ij}^{\theta}(v)-m_{ij}^{\theta}\cdot\nu_{ij}\bigr)+\sum_{ia}\kappa_{ia} A_{ia}.
$$
title: One conservative buffered separator and allocated section barycenters
